Patterns by Ear

Piano with a MIDI keyboard, no notation: learn the first tonal patterns of a set from finger numbers on the keys, then play the rest back by ear and see how many you got on the first try.

No notes on a staff here: patterns are learned from the keys and by listening. The first few patterns of a set are taught with finger numbers on an on-screen keyboard. Then the page plays the rest, one at a time, and you play each back on your keyboard.

Set up

Not connected. Chrome or Edge, keyboard plugged in by USB.

Sets you make on Tonal Patterns (Make a set) show up here with a ★.

Learn

Press Start above.

Blue keys and numbers: which keys, which finger (1 = thumb), and the small number above is the order. The page can hear the notes, not the fingers, so watch your hand.

By ear

Learn the first patterns, then come here.

The key is played first (I – V7 – I). Then each pattern: listen, then play it back. A wrong note stops the try and the pattern plays again. "Show me" and running out of tries count as a miss.

Results

Results show here when the by-ear patterns are done.

How it works

  • The sets. The same sets as Tonal Patterns: the stepwise and I–V sets, the 322–324 sets, and any set you make there. The first patterns of a set use the same chords as the rest, so learning them gives you the sound of each chord before you’re tested.
  • Fingering. The page works out the fingers itself. It keeps the hand in one position (no thumb-under, as these patterns are short), goes with the letter steps (C E G is 1 3 5), and keeps the thumb off black keys where it can. This is a rule of thumb, not taken from a method book: a teacher may prefer other fingers.
  • What counts. The notes in order. Rhythm and fingers are not checked. With Any octave counts on, the whole pattern may be an octave up or down. Stopping for more than four seconds starts the try again.
  • No MIDI keyboard? The computer keys play notes (bottom row white keys from Z = middle C, the row above black keys; ↑ ↓ change octave).
